solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Knight errant's boy suffering physical discomfort?

indicators.note: a person suffering a condition is in it, so the boy is placed inside the discomfort

blocks.note: a plain synonym
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A wandering knight's young squire seems to be aching all over after the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering' reads as an ordinary verb in the surface, but a boy suffering is a boy in pain: one word goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin was one of Charlemagne's peers, hence any chivalrous wandering knight in search of adventure.

clue.text: Shrewd Irish leader caught in a roomy environment

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front
an environment surrounds whatever lives in it, so the roomy word goes around the other letters

blocks.note: as in 'five pounds a head', a means per
a plain synonym
the opening letter of Irish
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A clever Irish politician is cornered somewhere with plenty of space around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' meaning per, as in 'ten pounds a head', is a less obvious use of the article; the two single letters go in after the second letter of the roomy word.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspicacious means having keen insight and understanding, which is what being shrewd amounts to.

clue.text: Greenery is a bore, invading shelter

indicators.note: invaders get inside a territory, so these words end up within the shelter

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
taken as written
in British English a fag is a tiresome chore

explanation.surface: Plants creeping into one's garden shed are a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag here is the British sense of a wearisome task, not a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage is foliage, the leaves of plants taken collectively, which makes up the greenery.

clue.text: Condescend to take up part of song I edited

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, a run of consecutive letters
in a down clue, taking something up lifts it from the bottom to the top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of song, I and the start of edited

explanation.surface: A singer stoops to perform a piece he has rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to do something one considers beneath one's dignity, which is condescending.

clue.text: Nourishing substance Greek character originally identified in river

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the first letter of the next word counts
one element sits inside the other, the river surrounding the selected letter

blocks.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
the Trent is a major English river
the first letter of identified

explanation.surface: A Greek scientist first spotted some nutritious compound in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is any substance that provides nourishment for growth and life.

clue.text: Old orator's initial itch for China tea

indicators.note: an initial is the opening letter of a word

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
the first letter of orator
to itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: An elderly speaker begins to crave a cup of Chinese tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Oolong is a partly fermented tea from China, between green and black tea.

clue.text: Live in, surprisingly coy about sports award

indicators.note: something turning out surprisingly is not as expected, so these letters come out in an unexpected order
about means around, so the rearranged letters wrap the award

blocks.note: rearranged
a cup is a trophy won in sport

explanation.surface: An athlete who is shy about a trophy unexpectedly lives with it on display.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy a house is to be resident in it, so the verb matches the phrasal verb live in.

clue.text: Report of only hotel in island, one demanding a lot of interest

definitions.text: one demanding a lot of interest

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the next word is wanted for its sound
one element is placed inside the island's name

blocks.note: only means lone, a word said the same as this spelling
Sark is one of the Channel Islands
Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H

explanation.surface: A news item about the island's single hotel mentions someone very keen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as someone who is very curious, but the interest is money charged on a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan shark lends money at extortionate rates, so he demands a lot of interest on it.

clue.text: Record plugging new melody, part of The Planets

indicators.note: a plug fills a gap, so the record is inserted into the words that follow

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
an EP is an extended-play record
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A recording promoting a fresh tune drawn from Holst's orchestral suite.
explanation.walkthrough: The Planets is Holst's orchestral suite, whose movements are named after planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune, the Mystic, is the final movement of Holst's suite The Planets.

clue.text: Level-headed about boxer's spasmodic twitching

blocks.note: re means concerning
Muhammad Ali, the boxer, with the possessive S
a tic is an involuntary muscular twitch

explanation.surface: A sensible remark about a fighter's nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A realistic person is practical and sensible about what can be achieved, which is being level-headed.

clue.text: Article on sacred river getting top grade

blocks.note: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's Kubla Khan
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An essay about a holy river earns the highest mark.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the article after the river. Coleridge's poem opens with 'Where Alph, the sacred river, ran', a fixed crossword reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha, the first Greek letter, is used for the best mark in British marking schemes.

clue.text: Poet and pontiff upholding a Roman law with hesitation

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding something up means sitting beneath it, so the pontiff comes after the other parts

blocks.note: taken as written
lex is Latin for law
a plain synonym
er is the sound of hesitating
the Pope is the supreme pontiff

explanation.surface: A poet and a pope both hesitantly support some ancient Roman statute.
explanation.walkthrough: The pontiff seems to be a second definition, especially as there were Popes named Alexander, but it supplies only the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was the eighteenth-century English poet of The Rape of the Lock and An Essay on Man.

clue.text: Quiet man finally consuming uncooked seafood

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word before it
to consume is to take in, so the outer letters swallow the next word

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction to play quietly
the final letter of man
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A shy man eventually eats raw shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn is a small edible crustacean, a common kind of seafood.

clue.text: The writer's attitude, assuming false identity

definitions.note: a gerund phrase used as a noun, matching the noun answer

blocks.note: the setter, the writer, refers to himself as I, and I'm is I am
a posture can be a mental stance or attitude

explanation.surface: An author explains that his pose involves pretending to be someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposture is the act of deceiving by pretending to be another person, as an impostor does.

clue.text: Native American's revolutionary directions inspiring strong desire

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the outer letters take in the desire

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary
north and east, two compass points
a yen is a yearning

explanation.surface: A tribesman's rebellious instructions stir a powerful longing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheyenne are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: New style English composer adopted with sincerity

indicators.note: a new version of the word is made by rearranging its letters
an adopted child is taken in, so the composer goes inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: rearranged
Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A fresh musical style was taken up wholeheartedly by an English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: English looks like it should give E, but it only describes the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something earnestly is to do it seriously and genuinely, which is acting sincerely.

clue.text: Device for recording time on river

blocks.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A gadget for logging how long a boat trip takes.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'time on river' puts the time after the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera records images, still or moving, so it is a recording device.

clue.text: Girl on river carrying minute percussion instrument

indicators.note: whatever is carried is held within, so the girl's name holds the next letter

blocks.note: a girl's name
M is the abbreviation for minute
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A girl by the river is holding a tiny drum.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Girl on river' puts the girl above, before the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A dulcimer is a stringed instrument played by striking the strings with small hammers, hence percussive.

clue.text: Copper given superb muscle relaxant once

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
rare can mean unusually fine

explanation.surface: A policeman is offered an excellent drug to relax his muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a policeman, but it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare, a plant poison used on arrows, was formerly given in surgery to relax muscles.

clue.text: He may steal two-fifths of stock kept by monarch, perhaps

indicators.note: two parts out of five means two letters of a five-letter word, here the opening pair
something kept is held inside, so the monarch's letters go around

blocks.note: a monarch is one example of a ruler
the first two of the five letters

explanation.surface: A king guards his livestock against a thief.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock fits the definition, since the thief takes livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals cattle or horses, so he is someone who may steal.

clue.text: Avoid little daughter's aquatic plant

blocks.note: to duck something is to dodge it
Scottish word for small
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Keep away from the small girl's pond plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Duckweed is a tiny floating plant covering the surface of ponds.

clue.text: Delightful Welsh girl supporting diocese

indicators.note: in a down clue a support is underneath, so the girl's name comes second

blocks.note: Ely is a Cambridgeshire cathedral city and diocese
Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A charming Welsh girl helps out her local church district.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysian means heavenly or blissful, from Elysium, the paradise of Greek myth.

clue.text: Castaway gloated in this way, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the words are taken for their sound

blocks.note: crowed means gloated, and so means in this way

explanation.surface: A shipwrecked man boasted like this, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe is Defoe's castaway marooned for years on a desert island.

clue.text: Ex-pupil's ruse mostly involving note to do with childbirth

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is kept, so its last letter is dropped
to involve is to include, so the outer letters take in the note

blocks.note: an OB, old boy, is a former pupil, with the possessive S
a plain synonym
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy's scheme involving a note to do with childbirth.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is the British term for a former pupil of a school; the note goes inside everything else, not just inside the ruse.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetric relates to obstetrics, the branch of medicine concerned with pregnancy and delivery.

clue.text: Customer's extra fiver ultimately securing uniform

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the extra wraps around the next letter
ultimately points at the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket
Uniform is the NATO alphabet word for U
the final letter of fiver

explanation.surface: A shopper's spare five-pound note goes towards a school uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored without the batter hitting the ball, counted among the extras.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyer is someone who purchases goods, so a customer.

clue.text: Show excessive pride in second-rate kiln

blocks.note: B is the grade below A, so second-class
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: A potter is too proud of a rather poor kiln.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast is to talk with excessive pride about one's own achievements or possessions.

clue.text: Divided up the port

blocks.note: first meaning: separated into parts
second meaning: a harbour city on the Croatian coast

explanation.surface: Someone carved up a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Split is a port city on Croatia's Dalmatian coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past participle for something divided and the name of a Croatian harbour city.

clue.text: Congenial girl mostly backed by counsel at first in court

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its last letter goes
backed means put into reverse, so the letters run the other way
at first points at the opening letter of the word before
one letter is placed inside the word for the court

blocks.note: a miss is a girl
a court can be an open paved yard, as a patio is
the first letter of counsel

explanation.surface: A pleasant young woman is supported by her lawyer in the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Court suggests a lawyer's setting, but here it is an open paved yard, and 'by' just sets the reversed girl beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico, borrowed from Italian, describes someone likeable and easy to get on with.

clue.text: Gannet regularly circling a chap's seaside defence

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
circling means going round, so the kept letters surround the chap

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters
a man's name

explanation.surface: A seabird keeps circling a man on the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A groyne is a low wall built out into the sea to check beach erosion, a coastal defence.

clue.text: Train soldiers, initially excluding detachment from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue reading from the east is reading right to left, so the word runs backwards
initially points at the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers
a detachment is a military unit
the first letter of excluding

explanation.surface: Soldiers are trained in the east, with one squad left out at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Train looks like a verb but is the noun: a train of attendants.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants following an important person, also called a train.
